Regulation: B.C. Reg. 123/2026
Made under: Utilities Commission Act
Published in: No. 13 – B.C. Regs. 110 to 124, July 14, 2026
Deposit date: July 10, 2026

B.C. Reg. 123/2026, deposited July 10, 2026, under theUTILITIES COMMISSION ACT[section 3]. Order in Council 298/2026, approved and ordered July 10, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that the attached Direction to the British Columbia Utilities Commission Respecting the Exemption of Independent Power Producers is made. — A. DIX,Minister of Energy and Climate Solutions; J. WICKENS,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. DIRECTION TO THE BRITISH COLUMBIA UTILITIESCOMMISSION RESPECTING THE EXEMPTION OFINDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCERS "Act"means theUtilities Commission Act; "independent power producer"means a person, or the successors or assigns of a person, who produces electricity and enters into an energy supply contract, within the meaning of section 68 of the Act, for the sale of electricity to Fortis. 2This direction is issued to the commission under section 3 of the Act. Exemption of independent power producers 3Within 10 days after the date this regulation comes into force, the commission must exercise its power under section 88 (3) of the Act to exempt independent power producers from Part 3, except section 22, of the Act in respect of (a)	the production of electricity and the sale of that electricity to Fortis, and (b)	the equipment, facilities, plant, projects or systems used for the production of electricity and the sale of that electricity to Fortis. minutes_briefs.title: BC exempts independent power producers from utility regulation when selling to Fortis
minutes_briefs.summary: The BC government has directed the BC Utilities Commission to exempt independent power producers (companies that generate electricity and sell it to Fortis, a major utility) from most of the rules in Part 3 of the Utilities Commission Act. This means these producers won't need to get approval for their rates or contracts, except for one section (section 22) that still applies. The exemption covers the production of electricity and the sale of that electricity to Fortis, including the equipment and facilities used. The commission must issue this exemption within 10 days after the regulation takes effect.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you are an independent power producer selling to Fortis, confirm with the BC Utilities Commission that your exemption is in place and review any remaining obligations under section 22.

key_dates.label: BC Utilities Commission must issue exemption for independent power producers
